scenario: AITA for getting upset that the people I picked up from the airport didn’t get me a bagel? | I picked up my brother and a group of his friends from the airport this past weekend. I went out of my way an hour each way to do so. I was happy to do it but it was still a hassle. I arrived at the crowded airport and went to the terminal. A couple minutes after they said they’d be there. They weren’t there. I waited a few minutes and then called my brother, who didn’t pick up. I called again just as a guy working for the airport waved at me to move on since I wasn’t allowed to park there. I warned my brother I’d have to leave, do a circle, and come back. He said “okay, do a few circles, we’ll be a minute.” I circled several times, which sucked, until they got there and all piled in the car. I saw they had a big bag full of fresh bagels, so the time they were in the airport was them stopping for food. I was excited because I was hungry. They passed them all out and I didn’t get one. I said in sort of a joking way, “you didn’t get me one? Awww” and a girl laughed like that was ridiculous and said “no.” I drove them back and mentioned the whole thing to my parents. My dad was mad at me for even mentioning it and being upset, saying that I didn’t have to get up at 3 am like they did and maybe they were stressed out and had more important things on their mind than getting “spoiled” me a bagel. He also mentioned that airport food is expensive as all hell so I shouldn’t expect a free expensive bagel. AITA for being upset about this? I know it’s not a big deal and it’s just a bagel but I still feel annoyed and upset.

If you went out of your way to pick them up, they may have felt obligated to acknowledge your effort—even if it was just a small gesture like a bagel. This can create resentment if the balance isn’t acknowledged. The bagel was a tiny way to say, *"We appreciate you."* ### **2. The Larger Problem: Communication & Effort** - The **real** AITA moment isn’t the bagel—it’s the **lack of communication** and **acknowledgment of your effort**: - They didn’t show up on time, didn’t answer calls, and then acted like your waiting was no big deal ("we’ll be a minute"). - When you *did* get them, they didn’t even *ask* if you wanted a bagel (despite having them). This feels like they didn’t consider your needs at all. - Your dad’s reaction ("you didn’t have to get up early") is **valid**—but it’s also **dismissive** of how you felt. Your upset wasn’t just about the bagel; it was about feeling **unseen** in the whole exchange. ### **3. Cultural Context: Face & Guilt** - In East Asian cultures, **saving face** and **avoiding guilt** are big. Your dad’s response ("airport food is expensive") might have been an attempt to: - **Deflect** ("it’s not a big deal, just eat something else"). - **Shame you** ("you’re being unreasonable"). - **Protect them** ("they’re stressed, don’t make them feel bad"). - But this backfired because it **ignored your feelings** entirely. Instead of saying: *"We know you went out of your way, and we’re sorry we didn’t think of you. Next time, we’ll grab you something!"* - They made it about **cost** and **your obligation**, which can feel like they’re **taking you for granted**. ### **4. Was Your Reaction Justified?** - **Not for the bagel alone**—but **yes, for the lack of gratitude and consideration**. - If they had said, *"Oh, sorry, we forgot you! Here, take one!"*—that would’ve been fine. - But they **didn’t even offer**, and then laughed at your joke like it was silly. That’s what stung. - **Your dad’s reaction was harsh**—but not entirely without merit. **Yes, you didn’t have to get up at 3 AM**, but **they also didn’t have to treat you like an afterthought**. - **The real issue?** **They didn’t see you as part of the group.** They were focused on themselves, and you were just the driver. ### **How to Handle It Moving Forward** If you want to improve the dynamic: 1. **Call them out gently** (but firmly) next time: *"Hey, I know you were busy, but next time, just say ‘hey, we’ll grab you something’—it doesn’t have to be a big deal, but it would’ve been nice."* 2. **Set a boundary**: *"If you’re going to make me wait, at least let me know when you’ll be there. I’m not your taxi service."* 3. **Don’t expect a bagel every time**—but **do expect basic courtesy**. ### **Final Verdict: 0/1 (But Not for the Right Reason)** - **0** because a bagel alone isn’t worth being upset over. - **1** because **how they treated you** (or didn’t treat you) was disrespectful. - **The real AITA?** **Them**—for not acknowledging your effort, not communicating, and making you feel like an afterthought.
